title: P02: quarter-original-rate Muon before the AdamW finish
description: P02 follow-up: halve peak split-QKV Muon LR again, from incumbent 0.01 to 0.005 (one quarter of the original 0.02), during the first 80% of pretraining. Smaller hidden-matrix updates may preserve reusable proof features and improve transfer through fixed downstream expert iteration, with the final 20% AdamW finish unchanged.
hypothesis: Muon (030) and a final 20% AdamW phase (032) improved all paired downstream seeds. Halving Muon LR to 0.01 in incumbent 034 improved the exact mean by 4 solves, but paired changes were -32/-20/+64, so evidence for a monotonic LR benefit is weak. Extending the AdamW finish in 033 did not improve the mean despite lower validation losses. No prior registration tests Muon LR 0.005. A further LR reduction may avoid disruption of learned proof features while retaining orthogonalized update geometry; alternatively it may undertrain the hidden matrices in the fixed 300-second budget. The derived Muon decay coefficient rises from 0.01 to 0.02 solely to preserve identical multiplicative shrinkage per update. Only downstream three-seed dev-transfer performance determines keep/discard.
expected_delta: Central prediction +2 to +12 dev-transfer solves at true length >=7 versus incumbent 034 exact mean 236.666667 (stored rounded 237); plausible downside -80 from undertraining. Auxiliary and final AdamW peak LR remains 0.001; switch stays at 240 seconds of 300. Operation counts, architecture and inference cost are identical, so no systematic per-step latency difference is expected and roughly 2900 updates should fit; learned generation lengths can alter total runtime under the fixed 1200-second cap.

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon hidden matrices then AdamW finish; continuous AdamW auxiliary

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: sqrt(max(1, rows/columns)) per orthogonalized matrix: Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 2, fc2 1
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW; muon_lr = 0.005 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: All 16 hidden projection parameters remain in Muon. Four qkv.weight matrices of shape (768,256) use independent Q/K/V updates, represented as a batch of three (256,256) matrices; proj/fc1/fc2 remain unchanged.
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each QKV update to (3,256,256); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. No extra learning-rate multiplier. Momentum and weight decay stay elementwise and unchanged.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, head.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters throughout; all hidden matrices additionally from elapsed fraction >=0.8
optimizer.decay_convention: Before switch, Muon lr*0.02 equals auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1, preserving incumbent shrinkage at each schedule fraction. After switch, all parameters use AdamW wd=0.1 at the existing auxiliary LR; integrated decay can differ with throughput.
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW

adamw_finish.parameters: all 16 hidden projection matrices added once to existing auxiliary AdamW optimizer
adamw_finish.lr: same scheduled auxiliary LR, nominal peak 0.001; no restart or additional warmup
adamw_finish.state: hidden matrices start fresh first/second moments; auxiliary state is retained
adamw_finish.muon_state: no Muon updates after switch; buffers local to pretrain only
